upstream.description: Strip multi-vendor AI provenance marks: Unicode text hygiene, statistical rewrite hooks, and C2PA/metadata from PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF/DOCX/HTML/MD

classification.analysis: watermarks-remover is an agent skill paired with a stdlib-only Python HTTP service that strips multi-vendor AI provenance marks — invisible Unicode artifacts, statistical text watermarks (SynthID-text, Kirchenbauer-style), and C2PA/EXIF/XMP metadata — from text and files (PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, and more). It ships as a thin agent skill (Claude, Cursor, Grok) that calls a local HTTP service over `/inspect`, `/detect`, and `/clean` endpoints, with Docker images bundling optional heavier detection backends (MarkLLM, MarkDiffusion, SynthID scorer). It's aimed at developers and privacy-conscious users who want to audit and clean AI-generation provenance markers from content they own, with explicit responsible-use documentation and fail-soft detection.

use_cases.title: Strip C2PA and EXIF provenance metadata from an AI-generated image
Detect and remove invisible Unicode watermarks from AI-written text
Run a local HTTP service to audit files for AI generation markers before publishing
